task.title: Diagnose and harden the portable release against Windows commit exhaustion
task.objective: Prove the cause of the v0.1.22 portable packaging failure, make the guarded packaging pipeline fail early with safe actionable resource diagnostics, preserve the real electron-builder exit code through release cleanup, and verify a genuine portable artifact when the host has sufficient commit headroom.

preserved_notes: The owner-created v0.1.22 version checkpoint at baseline commit 83198b43 is intentional evidence from the failed release and must not be reset, amended, or discarded.

writer.note: The v0.1.22 portable artifact and signed manifest now exist; project-state owns the exact success evidence, resolved environment block, and tracker reconciliation.

architecture: Keep the dashboard action on the canonical release-portable.ps1 to package-portable.ps1 pipeline.
Do not silently stop user services or applications; resource remediation must be explicit and operator-controlled.
Preserve the existing deterministic electron-builder compression policy unless evidence proves it is insufficient on an otherwise healthy release host.
security: Do not include account names, command lines, secrets, or process inventories in shipped error messages.
Do not alter signing-key custody or weaken manifest, provenance, fresh-state, or strict-offline gates.
compatibility: Windows PowerShell 5.1 remains supported and no administrator rights may be required for the resource preflight.
offline: No dependency, runtime download, network service, global Node, global Playwright, or global browser may be introduced.
Portable output and signed manifest behavior must remain compatible with the existing offline release contract.

acceptance.description: The v0.1.22 failure has timestamp-correlated operating-system evidence identifying the responsible resource boundary and child process.

Portable packaging checks free Windows commit immediately before electron-builder and fails early with a safe, actionable message when the available headroom is below the measured bounded-memory requirement.
A child packaging failure remains non-zero and the original exit code is reported after generated-file cleanup runs.
The fixed release scripts retain build, offline validation, signing, provenance, and genuine portable packaging behavior.
Authoritative roadmap sources remain consistent after the fix.

evidence.note: At 22:22:23 Windows diagnosed low virtual memory; oracle.exe consumed 5,753,339,904 bytes, comet.exe 1,983,148,032 bytes, and electron-builder's 7za.exe 685,993,984 bytes. This exactly matches the packaging failure window.

Negative-path acceptance passed: exit 1 after input validation with 717 MiB available of 32,556 MiB, a trusted [FAIL] label, 1,536 MiB minimum and pagefile/application/service remediation; build, manifest generation and electron-builder did not start.
175/175 after both in-memory negative controls; Overview reports Sources agree before final project-state reconciliation.
Application build completed successfully at v0.1.22 after the release-script changes.

Direct strict validation correctly rejected the restored v0.1.21 manifest after the v0.1.22 checkpoint. The canonical pipeline cannot regenerate it on this host until the 1,536 MiB commit preflight is satisfied; the original failed release had reached the packaging step, proving strict validation passed before 7za failed.

No v0.1.22 EXE was claimed. Current host has 717 MiB free Windows commit, below the measured 1,536 MiB floor; operator must close memory-heavy work or increase pagefile capacity before retrying npm run package:portable.

completion.note: The diagnostic and exit-code fixes are implemented and regression-proven. The fresh v0.1.22 artifact and strict current-manifest gate remain truthfully BLOCKED by host commit exhaustion; no service or user application was stopped without authorization.
